message.content:
{
  "pattern_id": "P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT",
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "rationale": "Add explicit job timeouts with operational headroom to both 'lint' and 'test' jobs. Baseline shows max workflow elapsed ~153s and sum job runtime ~265s, so per-job runtime likely under 3 minutes. Setting timeout-minutes: 5 (300s) provides ~2x headroom while bounding runaway executions. This preserves all existing steps, triggers, and required checks.",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: For each commit and PR
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    env:
      CGO_ENABLED: 1
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - name: Install Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@v3
      with:
        go-version-file: go.mod
    - name: make all-checks
      run: make all-checks
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    env:
      CGO_ENABLED: 1
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
      with:
        fetch-depth: 2
    - name: Install Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@v3
      with:
        go-version-file: go.mod
    - name: make all-tests
      run: make all-tests
    - name: upload codecov
      run: bash <(curl -s https://codecov.io/bash)
"
}
message.reasoning:
The user wants me to apply the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern to the given workflow. This pattern is about adding custom timeouts to jobs to bound their execution time.

Looking at the baseline records, I can see the workflow has two jobs: "lint" and "test". The workflow elapsed times are around 100-153 seconds, and sum job runtime seconds are around 189-265 seconds.

The pattern suggests choosing an explicit budget with operational headroom. I need to add timeout-minutes to each job. Since the longest job runtime in the baseline is around 265 seconds (about 4.4 minutes) for the sum of both jobs, and individual jobs likely take less time, I should set a reasonable timeout with headroom.

Looking at the workflow, both jobs run on ubuntu-latest. The lint job runs "make all-checks" and the test job runs "make all-tests" plus codecov upload.

I should add timeout-minutes to both jobs. A reasonable timeout might be 10 minutes (600 seconds) which gives plenty of headroom over the observed ~4-5 minute total runtime. But I should be more precise - since the sum is 265 seconds max, and there are two jobs running in parallel, each job probably takes around 2-3 minutes max. So 5 minutes (300 seconds) per job should be safe with headroom.

Actually, the workflow_elapsed_seconds is the wall-clock time (since jobs run in parallel), and sum_job_runtime_seconds is the sum of both jobs. So if workflow_elapsed is ~150s and sum is ~265s, each job averages ~130s. The max sum is 265s, so max per job might be around 150-200s. Adding 100% headroom would be 300-400s, so 5-7 minutes. I'll use 5 minutes (300 seconds) as timeout-minutes: 5.

Wait, timeout-minutes is in minutes, so 5 minutes = 300 seconds. That should be safe.

I need to add timeout-minutes to both jobs in the workflow YAML.
